changes.prefix: Run a probe outside a gate
changes.before: Run a probe outside a gate under `node scripts/harness.mjs bounded -- <command>`, one process at a time; the host guard also watches attributable session descendants.
changes.after: Run probes outside gates, one process at a time, under `node scripts/harness.mjs bounded -- <command>`; the host guard also watches attributable session descendants.

changes.before: Settle routine version, waiver-route, live-episode, regeneration and reinstall questions within existing authority; ask when the answer changes scope or authority.
changes.after: Resolve routine version, waiver-route, live-episode, regeneration and reinstall questions within existing authority; ask if an answer changes scope or authority.

changes.prefix: Before acting on an operator message
changes.before: Before acting on an operator message, state its aim in one line and act on that reading; ask one focused question if the reading is doubtful.
changes.after: Before acting on an operator message, state its aim in one line and act on that reading; ask one focused question if that reading is doubtful.

changes.before: A claim of cause, blocker, unreachable service or finished work names the command and output it rests on; a partial search names its boundary.
changes.after: Claims of cause, blockers, unreachable services or completion name their supporting command and output; partial searches name their boundary.

changes.before: Request needed authority in this session through the host permission flow; never hand the operator a command to run in your place unless the order or role names that fallback.
changes.after: Request needed authority here through the host permission flow; give the operator a command to run in your place only when the order or role names that fallback.

changes.prefix: A command given to the operator
changes.before: A command given to the operator is copy-paste runnable with real paths and no placeholders; a question says what it decides and why in plain words.
changes.after: Operator commands must be copy-paste runnable with real paths and no placeholders; questions plainly state what they decide and why.

changes.before: Answer a stale gate row by running the gate at the current identity, never by restoring bytes to match it; never remove a reviewed fix to pass a check.
changes.after: For stale gate rows, run the gate at the current identity; never restore bytes to match a row or remove a reviewed fix to pass a check.

changes.before: After a second consecutive provider safeguard refusal, stop retrying, record the stop as a decision naming phase and model, and resume in a fresh session.
changes.after: After two consecutive provider safeguard refusals, stop retrying, record a decision naming the stop, phase and model, and resume in a fresh session.

changes.before: Host permission settings decide execution; inspect the exact command, package mapping, and lifecycle-script diff before a state-changing resume command. In Claude Code the session hook records the dispatch named by the operator's phrase (`next`, `fix`, `verify`, `final-review`) before this procedure loads, delivers that command's briefing, passes a phrase whose dispatch is already recorded with the same briefing and receipt projected read-only by `npm run resume -- briefing` (a resumed Codex session runs that command itself), and reports a dispatch that is not legal in the current phase without rejecting the prompt. Prompt submission always remains open: setup, runtime and state failures are advisory, never a reason to deny access to Claude or Codex. It admits the dispatch exactly as the ordinary command: a live evidence gate or another session's writer reservation refuses it before any lifecycle change, and the terminal shows a one-line receipt naming the recorded dispatch and the equipped supports. Run no dispatch the harness recorded. Never repeat a recorded transition to repair a checkpoint warning.
changes.after: Host permissions decide execution; inspect the exact command, package mapping and lifecycle-script diff before any state-changing resume command. Before this procedure loads, Claude Code's session hook records the operator phrase's dispatch (`next`, `fix`, `verify`, `final-review`) and delivers its briefing. It passes an already-recorded phrase with the same briefing and receipt projected read-only by `npm run resume -- briefing`; resumed Codex runs that command itself. It reports an illegal dispatch without rejecting the prompt. Prompt submission stays open: setup, runtime and state failures are advisory, never grounds to deny access to Claude or Codex. Dispatch admission matches the ordinary command: a live evidence gate or another session's writer reservation refuses it before any lifecycle change. The terminal prints one receipt line naming the recorded dispatch and equipped supports. Never rerun a harness-recorded dispatch or repeat a recorded transition to repair a checkpoint warning.

changes.before: Completion flags: `--harness <harness> --harness-version <version> --model <model> --effort <level> --source <source>`. Supply each field; unknown is admitted. Versions, models and effort are logged, never refused, except that while Claude Code's `CLAUDE_EFFORT` is readable a claude-code attestation must be `--effort <that value> --source claude-session-readback`, and that source is refused anywhere else. `ultra` and `ultra code` record xhigh, mode subagents and raw spelling. Never invent effective-session readback. Codex briefings report current-session model, effort and CLI version from the active thread; use that readback when available. Claude Code exports the root session's selected effort as `CLAUDE_EFFORT`: the root session reads it and records that effort with `--source claude-session-readback` (selected, not effective); a subagent's shell carries the root's value, so the root session records lifecycle completions. Copilot readback reports CLI-selected values, not effective effort; retain supplied operator attestations and never derive the harness from the model.
changes.after: Completion flags: `--harness <harness> --harness-version <version> --model <model> --effort <level> --source <source>`. Supply each field; unknown is admitted. Versions, models and effort are logged, never refused, except for the Claude Code rule below. `ultra` and `ultra code` record xhigh, mode subagents and raw spelling. Never invent effective-session readback. Use available Codex briefing readback of current-session model, effort and CLI version from the active thread. Claude Code exports the root's selected effort as `CLAUDE_EFFORT`: when readable, the root must read and record it with `--effort <that value> --source claude-session-readback` in a claude-code attestation; that source is refused elsewhere. This is selected, not effective, effort; subagent shells carry the root's value, so the root records lifecycle completions. Copilot readback reports CLI-selected values, not effective effort; retain supplied operator attestations and never derive the harness from the model.

changes.before: Run checks that establish the work order's claims. Completion runs git diff --check inline, validates report/attestation presence and reads one judgment per declared criterion. An unmet criterion records and is shown at the next dispatch. A met npm test claim at executor or verifier handoff consumes the passing structural row, every --only suite named in the order's Preflight field and the document row when a document changed, all at the current code identity; a passing complete row also covers them. Final-review-result pass for a launchpad order with a met npm test claim consumes the newest passing complete review row at the integrated code identity, whichever role recorded it; a complete run is owed only when that identity has none. A met npm run test:docs claim consumes the newest passing document row recorded for the working tree as it stands; completion runs no gate itself. Target orders keep their target gate.
changes.after: Run checks establishing the work order's claims. Completion runs git diff --check inline, validates report/attestation presence, and reads one judgment per declared criterion. Unmet criteria are recorded and shown at the next dispatch. A met npm test claim at executor/verifier handoff consumes the passing structural row, every --only suite named in the order's Preflight field, and the document row if a document changed, all at the current code identity; a passing complete row covers them too. Final-review-result pass for a launchpad order's met npm test claim consumes the newest passing complete review row at the integrated code identity, whichever role recorded it; a complete run is owed only if that identity has none. A met npm run test:docs claim consumes the newest passing document row recorded for the working tree as it stands. Completion runs no gate. Target orders keep their target gate.

changes.prefix: Output reads, usage and planning handoffs
changes.before: Output reads, usage and planning handoffs advise. Review current authored outputs and record evidence with source and cutoff. Reports, indexes and release text may be completed after a passing gate without invalidating code identity. One registered writer owns a worktree on any branch. While its product gate runs, a role may write the active order’s own evidence, verification and final-review directories at the default document roots; product tasks reject observed reads of these paths. Every other gate input and the success record stay protected; document and mixed review gates admit no record writes; stop your own gate with `node scripts/harness.mjs evidence --stop` when necessary. Every other permission judgment delegates to the host. Read current authored outputs; generated or oversized outputs use their generation/check evidence. Codex lifecycle dispatches begin their harness session automatically before usage is read; Codex and Copilot can use explicit observe/delivered and `node scripts/harness.mjs read-output <path> --offset 0 --length 8192`, without claiming automatic read receipts. Copilot: inspect canonical status, run `npm run resume -- briefing` after an already-recorded dispatch, otherwise run the legal dispatch once; prompt-context delivery is unobserved. Completion releases its writer; explicit `scripts/operator-control.mjs` recovery remains available. Usage is recorded when available and unknown otherwise; it never blocks handoff.
changes.after: Output reads, usage and planning handoffs advise. Read and review current authored outputs; use generation/check evidence for generated or oversized outputs. Record evidence with source and cutoff. Reports, indexes and release text may be completed after a passing gate without invalidating code identity. One registered writer owns a worktree on any branch. During its product gate, a role may write the active order's own evidence, verification and final-review directories at the default document roots; product tasks reject observed reads there. Every other gate input and the success record stay protected; document and mixed review gates admit no record writes. Stop your own gate with `node scripts/harness.mjs evidence --stop` when necessary. Other permission judgments delegate to the host. Codex lifecycle dispatches automatically begin the harness session before usage is read. Codex and Copilot may use explicit observe/delivered and `node scripts/harness.mjs read-output <path> --offset 0 --length 8192`, without claiming automatic read receipts. Copilot: inspect canonical status; run `npm run resume -- briefing` after an already-recorded dispatch, otherwise run the legal dispatch once; prompt-context delivery is unobserved. Completion releases its writer; explicit `scripts/operator-control.mjs` recovery remains available. Record available usage, otherwise unknown; it never blocks handoff.

changes.prefix: Read source and existing tests relevant
changes.before: Read source and existing tests relevant to the order before changes. Scope those reads to `@subject-files`; unresolved paths remain a named input requirement.
changes.after: Before changes, read relevant source and existing tests within `@subject-files`; name unresolved paths as required inputs.

changes.prefix: Resolve physical cwd and Git root before
changes.before: Resolve physical cwd and Git root before changing files or running Git commands. Work only in the selected worktree; one writable coding agent owns it.
changes.after: Before file changes or Git commands, resolve physical cwd and Git root. Stay in the selected worktree with one writable coding agent.
